text: It is fair to say. <break time="0.8s" /> That patience has a terrible name. <break time="0.8s" /> For one thing. <break time="0.8s" /> The prospect of doing anything that you have been told will require patience. <break time="0.8s" /> Simply seems unattractive. <break time="0.8s" /> More specifically, though. <break time="0.8s" /> It is disturbingly passive. <break time="0.8s" /> It is the virtue. <break time="0.8s" /> That has traditionally been urged upon housewives. <break time="0.8s" /> While their husbands led more exciting lives outside the home. <break time="0.8s" /> Or on racial minorities. <break time="0.8s" /> Told to wait just a few more decades. <break time="0.8s" /> For their full civil rights. <break time="0.8s" /> The talented but self effacing employee who waits patiently for a promotion. <break time="0.8s" /> We tend to feel. <break time="0.8s" /> Will be waiting a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> She ought to be trumpeting her achievements instead. <break time="0.8s" /> In all such cases. <break time="0.8s" /> Patience is a way of psychologically accommodating yourself. <break time="0.8s" /> To a lack of power. <break time="0.8s" /> An attitude intended to help you. <break time="0.8s" /> To resign yourself to your lowly position. <break time="0.8s" /> In theoretical hopes of better days to come. <break time="0.8s" /> But as society accelerates. <break time="0.8s" /> Something shifts. <break time="0.8s" /> In more and more contexts. <break time="0.8s" /> Patience becomes a form of power. <break time="0.8s" /> In a world geared for hurry. <break time="0.8s" /> The capacity to resist the urge to hurry. <break time="0.8s" /> , to allow things to take the time they take. <break time="0.8s" /> Is a way to gain purchase on the world. <break time="0.8s" /> To do the work that counts. <break time="0.8s" /> And to derive satisfaction from the doing itself. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of putting off all your fulfillment to the future.
